This means Alaska's full-year revenue and expense figures are not a clean full-year, single-entity comparison in the same way Delta, United, Southwest, and American's are (a full four quarters of a single consolidated entity). Bearing that caveat in mind, here are the calculations from the reported FY2024 figures [DOC-1]:

**Aircraft fuel expense as % of revenue (FY2024):**
- Delta: 10,566 / 61,643 = 17.14%
- United: 11,756 / 57,063 = 20.60%
- American: 11,418 / 54,211 = 21.06%
- Southwest: 5,812 / 27,483 = 21.15%
- Alaska: 2,506 / 11,735 = 21.36%

Ranking (lowest to highest): **Delta < United < American < Southwest < Alaska**

**Salaries, wages and benefits as % of revenue (FY2024):**
- Delta: 16,161 / 61,643 = 26.22%
- United: 16,678 / 57,063 = 29.23%
- American: 16,021 / 54,211 = 29.55%
- Alaska: 3,588 / 11,735 = 30.58%
- Southwest: 12,240 / 27,483 = 44.54%

Ranking (lowest to highest): **Delta < United < American < Alaska < Southwest**

**Comparison of rankings:** Delta ranks lowest (best, i.e., most favorable/lowest cost ratio) in both metrics — lowest fuel expense as a % of revenue and lowest salaries/wages/benefits as a % of revenue. So yes, the top-ranked (lowest-cost-ratio) airline is the same — Delta — in both rankings, though the ordering of the remaining four airlines differs between the two metrics (notably Southwest, which is 4th-lowest in fuel% but highest in salaries%, and Alaska, which is highest in fuel% but not highest in salaries%, subject to the comparability caveat noted above regarding its partial-year Hawaiian consolidation).

ANSWER: Yes — Delta Air Lines ranks lowest (1st) in both fuel expense-to-revenue (17.14%) and salaries/wages/benefits-to-revenue (26.22%). Full ranking (lowest to highest): Fuel% — Delta, United, American, Southwest, Alaska; Salaries% — Delta, United, American, Alaska, Southwest. Note: Alaska's figures are not fully comparable to the others since they include Hawaiian Holdings only from the Sept. 18, 2024 acquisition date onward.
